decision.analysis: Round 3 (final) analysis. The prior results clearly establish resnet18 (depth=3, hidden=32, lr=0.0005, hflip+vflip, standardize) as the top performer at 99.16% validation accuracy / 99.17% balanced accuracy. The residual_cnn follows at 97.56%, vision_transformer at 96.07%, compact_transformer at 94.76%, and tiny_cnn at 93.13%. Key patterns: (1) standardize normalization is universal across all configs; (2) adamw + cosine + weight_decay=0.0001 is the consistent optimizer stack; (3) batch_size=128 works well; (4) label_smoothing=0.05 is standard; (5) hflip is the most common augmentation, with vflip adding a small boost for resnet18. The compact_transformer underperformed likely due to under-capacity (hidden=48, depth=2) and attention pooling adding variance. For this final round, I will: (A) push the resnet18 with moderate capacity increase (depth 3→4, hidden 32→48) and a slightly lower LR (0.0005→0.0003) for stable convergence with more parameters, plus adding rotate90 as a third conservative geometric augmentation; (B) retry the compact_transformer with substantially more capacity (hidden 48→96, depth 2→4) and simpler cls pooling to test whether the architecture can close the gap when properly sized. Both configs stay within the 1-4M parameter budget and use conservative regularization appropriate for 90K samples.

candidates.rationale: Building on the best prior result (resnet18 depth=3, hidden=32, lr=0.0005 → 99.16% acc), this candidate increases capacity moderately: depth 3→4 adds one more residual block for richer feature hierarchy, and hidden 32→48 widens channels by 50% to capture more discriminative pathology features. The LR is reduced to 0.0003 to maintain training stability with the larger parameter count (roughly 1.5-2x more params). rotate90 is added as a third conservative geometric augmentation (alongside hflip and vflip) to provide orientation invariance without destroying tissue-orientation cues. All other hyperparameters (adamw, cosine, wd=1e-4, ls=0.05, batch=128, dropout=0.1, standardize) are held constant to isolate the effect of the capacity and augmentation changes. The 1.63x class imbalance is mild enough that class_weighting is unnecessary; label_smoothing=0.05 provides sufficient regularization.

The prior compact_transformer (hidden=48, depth=2, attention pooling) scored only 94.76%, likely under-capacity for the task. This retry doubles hidden to 96 (divisible by num_heads=4, multiple of 8) and quadruples depth to 4, giving the conv tokenizer and attention blocks substantially more expressiveness while staying within the ~2-3M parameter budget. Switching from attention pooling to cls pooling reduces variance in the readout and simplifies the classification head. LR is set to 0.0003 (lower than the prior 0.0005) for stable convergence with the larger model. hflip+vflip provide conservative geometric augmentation. The conv tokenizer (patch_size=4, tokenizer_layers=2) maps 28x28x3 to a 7x7 grid of 49 tokens at dim 96, preserving local histological texture before 4 full-attention layers model global tissue context. This tests whether a properly-sized compact_transformer can approach the CNN baselines on PathMNIST.
